sources.title: Executive Order 12036 - United States Intelligence Activities (24 January 1978)

claims.text: Signed 'JIMMY CARTER / The White House, / January 24, 1978' and filed with the Office of the Federal Register at 11:19 a.m. on 25 January 1978. Section 4-101 supersedes 'Executive Order 11905, United States Foreign Intelligence Activities, dated February 18, 1976', together with EOs 11985 and 11994.

sources.title: Executive Order 12036 - United States Intelligence Activities (24 January 1978)

claims.text: Section 1-302: 'The SCC shall consider and submit to the President a policy recommendation, including all dissents, on each special activity.' Section 4-212 defines a special activity as an activity conducted abroad in support of foreign policy objectives where the role of the United States Government 'is not apparent or acknowledged publicly.'

sources.title: Executive Order 12036 - United States Intelligence Activities (24 January 1978)

claims.text: Section 3-401 requires the congressional intelligence committees to be kept 'fully and currently informed', and expressly states that this is 'not... a condition precedent'. Being told is not a prerequisite to acting.

sources.title: Executive Order 12036 - United States Intelligence Activities (24 January 1978)

claims.text: Section 3 builds a four-part oversight structure: an Intelligence Oversight Board of three members from outside government but inside the White House (3-1), agency Inspectors General and General Counsel (3-2), the Attorney General (3-3), and the congressional committees (3-4).

claims.text: DO NOT CITE THIS ORDER FOR COMPARTMENTATION. The words 'compartment', 'special access' and 'need-to-know' appear zero times in the text. The nearest provision is section 4-106, which only says implementing documents will sometimes be classified.

connections.edgeLabel: Routes every special activity to the President through an NSC committee
connections.label: National Security Council
connections.note: Section 1-302: 'The SCC shall consider and submit to the President a policy recommendation, including all dissents, on each special activity.' Section 4-212 defines a special activity by the concealment of the United States role, not by its content.

connections.edgeLabel: Fully and currently informed, and expressly not a condition precedent
connections.label: Congressional oversight of special access programs
connections.note: Section 3-401 requires the congressional intelligence committees to be kept 'fully and currently informed' while stating that this is 'not... a condition precedent'. Notification is owed; permission is not.

desc: Carter's intelligence charter order. It is on this board for its special-activity approval chain and its oversight structure, and for a negative finding: it contains no compartmentation provision of any kind, so it cannot be cited for one.
